analysis:
The PR changes docs/provider/cli-reference.md only. The supplied units are BASE text (lines 1-404 and 405-821), and the patch excerpt is truncated. The visible changes are: the date bump at line 3; the clarification at line 52 that GLM video input accepts constant or variable frame rate; a new warning at lines 178-180 (head) that a selection serving GLM-5.3-Flash below the macOS GPU wired-memory limits prints `warning:` and continues; and further edits at head ranges 949-952, 1100-1130, 1615 and 1641 that are not visible in the supplied units. The 949-952 edit appears to alter the live daemon status description, and the remaining ranges, including a likely new wired-memory section, are only partly visible.

No code, config, protocol or authorization behavior changes in the visible material. The documented warning is non-blocking and advisory. It is an availability/performance note, not a security control, and it does not affect the attestation, authorization, key custody or cache-storage entries (T-041, T-053, A-008). Existing logout, cache and Autopilot descriptions in the base text are unchanged in the visible patch.

Limits on this conclusion: the head text was not supplied, the patch excerpt is incomplete, and the claims about the anchor `#glm-53-flash-gpu-wired-memory-limit` and the warning behavior in provider-swift code are unverified. Doc-only drift is not a security regression. Any accompanying provider-swift source change (warning logic, VFR video decoding) is outside this batch, and the VFR video path could touch temporary-file handling (T-050) if the source changed. I recommend that the source-bearing batches be reviewed for that.
